message:
fix(cli): parse capture and grade-compare --timeout as a duration (#7715)

capture read --timeout with parseInt, so `--timeout 1s` became a 1 ms
page-load timeout. grade-compare dropped an invalid value without a
warning. Both now use the shared parseTimeoutMs helper that check and
snapshot already use, keeping their defaults of 120000 ms and 5000 ms.

Fixes #7671

docs(cli): list --format and the 24-worker cap in docs rendering (#7716)

`hyperframes docs rendering` said workers run 1-8, but the engine
clamps an explicit value to 24, and it never mentioned --format or
--gif-loop. The options now match render.ts and the engine limit.

Fixes #7668

feat(studio): toasts show as a centred pill that rises in (#7714)

* feat(studio): toasts show as a centred pill that rises in

* fix(studio): error toasts stay up on a click so their text can be copied

fix(lint): say the audio overlap warning is about a shared Studio lane (#7700)

duplicate_audio_track said two overlapping clips on one data-track-index
"cause layered audio playback" and suggested moving one to another track.
The render's mixer never reads data-track-index (every audible clip is its own
amix input) and the docs call the attribute a Studio lane only, so the two
clips are layered whatever their tracks: rendering a whoosh and a hit on
track 6, then with the hit on track 7, gives byte-identical audio. The message
now says both play and that the overlap is two clips sharing one Studio lane;
the hint says splitting tracks leaves the mix unchanged, and that a leftover
duplicate should be removed or moved. lint-rules.mdx said the audio "doubles
up"; it now says the same as the message.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cli): quote the project name in init's printed `cd` commands (#7608)

`hyperframes init --non-interactive` closes with `cd <name> && npm run …`
lines for the person or agent to paste. The name went in as typed, so a
name with a space or a quote printed a command that fails as written:
`cd my first video` (bash: "cd: my: No such file or directory", zsh: "too
many arguments") and `cd it's mine` (an unterminated quote).

A new `shellArg` quotes a word only when a shell would split or expand
it: double quotes, or single quotes when the text holds `$`, a backtick,
`\`, `"` or `!`; on Windows, double quotes, with `\` paths left bare.
`hyperframes open` / `preview --stop` hints (desktopApp's `shownDir`)
already quoted whitespace with JSON.stringify and now use it too, so a
name like `it's` or `a&b` is covered there as well.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cli): the render header names the quality preset and CRF it encodes with (#7697)

The settings line printed the encoder tier, so the default render said
"30fps · standard · …" while it encoded the looks preset at CRF 16, and
-q delivery said "high". A long-form render that came out at ~40 Mbps
read as "standard quality" in its own log.

The line now prints the --quality name as asked for and the CRF or
bitrate in effect: "looks (CRF 16)" by default, "looks (CRF 20)" with
--crf 20, "looks (10M)" with --video-bitrate 10M, "draft", "delivery".

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(check): name a color-graded video by its own selector in layout findings (#7699)

A color-graded <video> is painted into a canvas the runtime inserts after it,
with a runtime-generated id (__hf_color_grading_<video id>). Layout findings on
that canvas (e.g. container_overflow for a punch-in inside an overflow:hidden
box) named the canvas, so the fix hint "mark intentional overflow with
data-layout-allow-overflow" pointed at an element the author never wrote.
The audit already reads flags from the authored video (authoredElement);
uniqueSelectorFor now names that element too, so the finding's selector,
data attributes and source file are the video's.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
